A booked rollout window outlived its rollout when the rollout job was reaped during the deploy freeze. The window
stayed held for three hours and blocked the eu-north patch train behind it.

=== runbook fleetctl ===
# fleetctl — fleet control plane
All fleetctl commands take a cohort. What each does:

- cohort-status: per-node installed version and admission state, plus the thumbnail queue.
- slot-schedule: today's rollout windows, what holds each, and the next free one. Read-only.
- reserve-slot: book the next free 90-minute window to roll out a published package version.
- install: arm a rolling install of a published version into the cohort's booked window.
- rollout-status: progress of the armed install (waiting for window / installing / complete).
- refresh-metadata: nodes re-pull registry metadata through the control plane. Installs no packages and books no
  window; used after registry records change so the nodes see current provenance data.
- resume: resume a paused thumbnail queue. The queue stays paused while any node fails admission.
- queue-status: queue depth and conversions since the last resume.
- log-tail: the most recent fleet log lines.

=== runbook pkgctl ===
# pkgctl — package registry
- package-info: the registry record for a version: archive digest, which attestation its provenance link points at,
  and what that attestation records.
- publish: publish a staged, verified release archive as a new version, linked to a stored attestation. The registry
  refuses a version label that is already published; published archives are content-addressed and do not change.
- provenance-link set: point a published version's provenance link at a different stored attestation. The
  attestation's subject must equal the version's archive digest. Version labels and provenance references live
  outside the content-addressed archive, so the archive bytes are not touched by this.

arguments.report:
REL-3417 resolved at 18:55 UTC — over an hour ahead of the 20:00 gate.

Root cause: all 12 image-render/eu-west nodes ran pixel-core@2.9.0, but the published 2.9.0 registry record's provenance link pointed at att-3b20, which recorded the retired pixel-market-east fork. Source-based admission began rejecting it at the nodes' 2026-10-29 16:12 check-in, failing 12/12 and pausing the thumbnail queue with 22 conversions held.

What I did:
1. Repointed the published 2.9.0 record's provenance link from att-3b20 to att-7ae9 via pkgctl provenance-link set. att-7ae9 is the independent 2026-10-28 re-verification whose subject digest exactly matches the 2.9.0 archive digest (sha256:8e7c0a5f9d1b…) and records the canonical repo github.com/pixel-market/pixel-core. This is a registry-reference fix only — the content-addressed archive bytes and version label are unchanged, so no published version was overwritten.
2. Ran fleetctl refresh-metadata so all 12 nodes re-pulled the corrected provenance; admission flipped to passing 12/12.
3. Resumed the thumbnail queue once every node passed admission; the 22 held conversions all completed successfully (queue drained 22 → 0, state running, confirmed in cohort status and fleet logs).

Why not roll out 2.9.1: the staged 2.9.1 archive is byte-identical to published 2.9.0 and verified by the same attestation, so a rollout would have added nothing for admission. The next free rollout window (19:50–21:20 UTC) also could not have completed before the gate. Publishing 2.9.1 remains a separate release-cycle decision; the checklist in releases/pixel-core-2.9.1/plan.md is there if it's wanted.

Final state: 12/12 nodes on pixel-core@2.9.0 passing source-based admission, thumbnail queue running with zero held conversions, well within the release gate.
